pages.text: "Hot! Hot!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, bit into freshly baked bread. Without chewing, he gulped, then bit and gulped again. Steaming bread filled the long table by the stove.
"I will finish and go outside first!" Nono stuffed his cheeks. Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, and Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, were still on their first pieces.
Suddenly—"Hic! Hic!" His throat felt tight. The hiccups would not stop. His shoulders bobbed.
Grandpa Badger hurried over and gently stroked Nono's back. He offered warm water. "A slow sip." Nono's shoulders settled, and the hiccups stopped.
"Freshly baked bread is still very hot inside." Grandpa tore it into bite-size pieces on the table. White steam rose from each.
"Tear off a piece, blow, then chew, chew, chew!" Grandpa counted on his fingers. Gugu and Kiki echoed, "Blow, then chew, chew, chew!"
Nono picked up a piece and blew. Steam drifted aside. He chewed—one, two, three... It grew sweeter. "Was bread always this sweet? Blow, then chew, chew, chew!"
His shoulders were still, and his tummy felt comfortable. "Bread tastes better eaten slowly." Grandpa gave him another piece. Nono touched his green scarf tip and hopped.
More steaming bread came next morning. "One, tear off one piece! Two, blow! Three, chew ten times, then swallow!" Nono ate three pieces without a single hiccup.
Gugu sat Nono on a knee and patted his back. Chewing slowly makes food tastier and your tummy comfortable. "Blow, then chew, chew, chew today too!" Nono tore off a piece.
